To reminisce is to indulge in the enjoyable recollection of past events. It’s more than just "remembering"; it’s the act of mentally revisiting memories, often with a sense of nostalgia or affection.

Key Characteristics

  • The Tone: Usually positive or bittersweet. You generally don't "reminisce" about a dental appointment or a stressful meeting; you reminisce about "the good old days," old friends, or significant life milestones.
  • The Action: It often involves sharing those memories with others—like sitting around a table telling stories—but you can also reminisce privately.
  • The Feeling: It’s closely tied to nostalgia. While remembering is a functional brain process (e.g., remembering where you put your keys), reminiscing is an emotional one.

Examples in Context

  • "The two veterans sat on the porch to reminisce about their time stationed overseas."
  • "After graduation, we spent the whole night reminiscing about our favorite professors and the late-night study sessions."
  • "Looking through old photo albums always makes me want to reminisce about my childhood."

Word Origin

It comes from the Latin re- (again) and mens (the mind). Essentially, you are "bringing it to mind again."
